So the only unique bytes were cursor and handover scaffolding. Caveat recorded with the numbers rather than after them: blob existence proves no file holds NOVEL content, not that each file matches the revision the worktree was cut at.

MECHANICS THE SUCCESSOR WILL NEED, learned the hard way four times today. git worktree remove on a review worktree here DELETES THE ADMIN DIR FIRST AND THEN FAILS with Permission denied on read-only pack/cache trees, so the worktree ends up deregistered with its directory left behind; the sequence that works is git worktree remove, then chmod -R u+w, then rm -rf, then git worktree prune. Reaching the delete step at all is itself the clean-tree check, because git refuses a worktree with modified or untracked files first. The ownership guard REFUSES git -C <worktree> status (a git subcommand outside the declared roots) while ALLOWING git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD.
